Specifically, achieved calling help function flip. flip function defined follows: Bernoulli probability distribution binary outcome space, represented Boolean variable taking values TRUE FALSE. appropriate probability distribution coin flipping. single parameter Bernoulli distribution, called probability flip function, assumed convention probability obtaining outcome TRUE. case, probability obtaining heads. observe statement weights simulation likelihood observing particlar data point Bernoulli distribution. completes TreePPL description coin flipping model. code: sampler <- tp_compile("coin") readr::read_file(sampler$model_path) model function coinModel(coinflips: Bool[]) => Real  {   // Uncomment if you want to test the input   //printLn("Input:");   //let coinStr = apply(bool2string, coinflips);   //printLn(join(coinStr));   assume p ~ Beta(2.0, 2.0); // prior   let n = length(coinflips);   for i in 1 to n {     flip(coinflips[i], p); // likelihood   }   return(p); // posterior } function flip(datapoint: Bool, probability: Real) {   observe datapoint ~ Bernoulli(probability); }

TreePPL writes NaN infinite values {"__float__": "nan"}; read R's NaN, Inf -Inf. MCMC weights equal, returned. Parameters named fields model's return type output (e.g. lambda, mu), x1, x2, ... otherwise. Non-scalar values (vectors, trees) kept list-columns.
